articles.text:
Khaime raises $500,000 pre-seed funding to build the future of AI-powered commerce
0
By
Tapiwa Matthew Mutisi
on
November 19, 2026
Artificial Intelligence , Business , Ecommerce , Funding , News , Startups
Khaime, a next-generation commerce platform designed specifically for the emerging era of AI-driven shopping, has secured $500,000 in pre-seed funding. The investment round was led by Launch Africa Ventures , with additional participation from angel investors and the company’s early friends-and-family backers.
The funding comes at a time when artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming online commerce, introducing a future where AI agents, rather than humans, increasingly search for products, compare prices, negotiate purchases, and complete transactions on behalf of consumers.
Building Stores for AI Shoppers
Founded and led by Gabriel Olokunwolu, Khaime is positioning itself at the intersection of e-commerce and artificial intelligence. Unlike conventional online stores built solely for human customers, Khaime is designed to support both human buyers and AI-powered shopping agents operating on users’ behalf.
The company believes that commerce is entering a new phase where intelligent agents will become key participants in the purchasing process. As a result, merchants will need platforms that can communicate, negotiate, and transact seamlessly with these AI systems.
According to Adeola Adedewe , CEO of Kredete, this shift is already underway.
We talk a lot about the next customer not being human. In commerce, that is already starting: agents shop, compare and pay for us. Khaime is building the stores they can buy from.
An AI-Native Commerce Platform
Khaime’s platform enables merchants to sell to customers globally while supporting a wide range of payment preferences and currencies. The platform currently supports more than 120 currencies and integrates local payment options, allowing consumers to pay using familiar methods regardless of their location.
At the heart of the platform is Khai, Khaime’s proprietary AI shopping and sales assistant.
Khai is designed to help businesses automate key aspects of customer engagement and sales operations by:
Managing customer conversations
Converting chats into completed purchases
Following up on abandoned carts
Recovering potentially lost sales
Providing automated support throughout the buying process
Importantly, merchants remain in control. Businesses can define specific rules and parameters governing how Khai interacts with customers and manages transactions.
Helping Merchants Become Discoverable in the AI Economy
As AI increasingly influences how consumers find products and services, Khaime is helping businesses prepare for a future where visibility extends beyond traditional search engines.
The platform assigns every online store a discoverability score, which evaluates how easily merchants can be found by both search engines and AI assistants. Khaime then provides actionable recommendations in plain language, helping businesses improve their visibility and increase their chances of appearing in AI-generated shopping recommendations.
This functionality addresses what industry experts see as a growing challenge: ensuring merchants are discoverable not only by human customers but also by intelligent agents making purchasing decisions.

articles.title: Cyient Semiconductors Secures $10 Mn Investment From GlobalFoundries
articles.snippet: Cyient Semiconductors Secures $10 Mn Investment From GlobalFoundries Analytics India Magazine
articles.text:
Key takeaways
Cyient Semiconductors has secured a $10 million investment from GlobalFoundries, valuing the company at $510 million.
The funding will enhance Cyient's custom silicon and ASIC capabilities, improving supply chain resilience and manufacturing access.
This investment is seen as a validation of India's semiconductor innovation potential, strengthening its position in the global market.
Cyient aims to contribute to semiconductor design and product development across various industries, including automotive and AI.
The partnership with GlobalFoundries is expected to support Cyient's long-term growth and global customer engagements.
Takeaways drafted with AI from the article text.
Cyient Semiconductors has approved a $10 million equity investment from US-based chipmaker GlobalFoundries (GF). The transaction will take place at a pre-money valuation of $490 million.
It follows Cyient Semiconductors' recent funding round led by Edelweiss. The combined investment values the company at a $510 million post-money valuation.
Cyient Semiconductors plans to use the investment to expand its turnkey custom application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) capabilities. It will also accelerate custom silicon development and strengthen long-term wafer supply assurance. The company expects the partnership to improve supply chain resilience and access to advanced manufacturing capabilities.
"This investment is a strong validation of our vision and the opportunity ahead for semiconductor innovation from India," Suman Narayan, CEO of Cyient Semiconductors, said in a statement.
The investment comes as India seeks to strengthen its position in the global semiconductor value chain. Cyient aims to contribute through semiconductor design , product development, and intellectual property creation in India. The company serves customers across automotive, industrial, AI, communications, and data centre markets.
Narayan said the investment would help accelerate innovation and strengthen the company's engineering capabilities. It would also support its global customer engagements and long-term growth strategy.
"Having a leading semiconductor ecosystem partner as a strategic investor validates our technology and business model," he added.
Cyient Semiconductors provides custom ASIC and application-specific standard product (ASSP) solutions. Its capabilities cover chip architecture, design, manufacturing, packaging, testing, and qualification. The company also focuses on analogue mixed-signal technology, intelligent power and advanced semiconductor platforms.
It operates design centres in India, Belgium, and the US. Its customers include companies in data centres, robotics, automotive, and industrial automation.

articles.title: RHISE AI Launches European Personal AI Platform Lucie

RHISE AI has raised an angel round from more than 40 investors to develop Lucie, a personal AI platform connecting health, professional, and personal information.

articles.text:
RHISE AI Launches European Personal AI Platform Lucie
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 1:33 PM
RHISE AI Launches European Personal AI Platform Lucie
RHISE AI has raised an angel round from more than 40 investors to develop Lucie, a personal AI platform connecting health, professional, and personal information.
Investors include Prince Max von und zu Liechtenstein, Dr. Klaus Kleinfeld, Raoul Heraeus, and Michael Baum. The round’s financial size was not disclosed.
Lucie is available on iPhone and Mac in English and German.
Proactive Personal Assistance
Lucie can connect information from calendars, inboxes, and wearable health devices. RHISE AI’s internally developed Heartbeat multi-agent system works in the background to identify items requiring attention, recommend next steps, and act after receiving user approval.
More than half of Lucie’s active users have connected live health information from a wearable device.
RHISE AI says personal information is hosted on European cloud infrastructure in Germany and is not sold.
The company was founded by Andy Loy, previously the founder of industrial AI company KONUX, alongside Danil Gontovnik, Samy Samandjeu, and Chris Seybold.
KEY QUOTES:
Personal AI will soon know more about us than any technology before it. The question is who it works for. Most of it is being built to capture attention. Everyone in this round has built something that lasted, and everyone in it wants Europe to build this category, not rent it.
Andy Loy, Co-Founder and CEO of RHISE AI
Most AI waits to be asked. Lucie works in the background, so you don’t have to carry everything in your head. It suggests what to do, and nothing happens without your say.
Danil Gontovnik, Co-Founder and CTO of RHISE AI
Industrial AI showed what European engineering can do. Now this team is bringing the same rigour to the most personal technology of all.
Dr. Klaus Kleinfeld, Former CEO of Siemens, Alcoa, and NEOM
European society deserves sovereign AI that serves people and does not consume them.
Prince Max von und zu Liechtenstein, CEO of LGT
I’ve spent 35 years building and backing technology that wanted more of people’s time. Lucie gives it back. I invested, and I use it daily.
Michael Baum, Founding CEO of Splunk
Our future will be shaped more and more by technology. But true progress means making sure humanity benefits from it, rather than losing what makes us human. I believe technology should empower us to reconnect with ourselves, with each other, and with what truly matters. That’s why I believe in Lucie.
Raoul Heraeus, Managing Partner of ALERA Capital
